## 3. The evidence that moved it










**"Virtual cell" is in a *Cell* title in December 2024.** [39672099](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39672099/): how to
build the virtual cell with artificial intelligence — priorities and
opportunities. This corpus has now dated the arrival of that vocabulary three
times: 2025-11, then 2025-04 after the first backfill, and now 2024-12. Each
date was the earliest month then being read. The honest conclusion is not a
fourth date but the retirement of the question.

**AI agents reach an oncology journal in December 2024, not June 2025.**
[39690222](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39690222/) (*Nat Cancer*): how AI agents will change cancer research and
oncology, a three-page comment over five named authors. The corpus's dated
diffusion chain — general and methods bench in February 2025, oncology in June,
immunology in December, "ten months" — is wrong at its origin and wrong at its
oncology waypoint. Both move back about six months, and the lag it measured was
an artefact of where reading began.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph paired the comment with [39690213](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39690213/), "foundation models in
    clinical oncology", "published in the same issue" — which reads as two
    independent statements arriving together. It is a single-page research
    highlight on page 1790, written by one journal editor, with no abstract and
    no reference list, summarising work published elsewhere. A journal's own
    front matter is not a second voice on the subject the journal is covering,
    and the waypoint above rests on the comment alone. That card is now
    `neutral`.

**Agents doing production work.** [39718779](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39718779/): an LLM-assisted workflow mines
thousands of enzyme-substrate interactions from published manuscripts. Not a
demonstration and not a benchmark — a literature-scale extraction job.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nothing lands on a tracked thread this month.

### (b) Method credibility

[39313595](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39313595/) (*Nat Med*): a toolbox for surfacing health-equity harms and
biases in large language models. December 2024 has, in the same month, the
virtual-cell manifesto, the AI-agents-in-oncology comment, a drug-repurposing
foundation model ([39322717](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39322717/), TxGNN) and this harms toolbox. The enthusiasm
and the audit are not separated in time anywhere in this corpus once the window
is wide enough to check, and every claim this corpus has made about a lag between
them has been withdrawn.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This sentence counted "three drug-repurposing foundation models" and cited
    two PMIDs for them. There is one. [39448863](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39448863/) is a two-page *Nature
    Medicine* News & Views, pages 3422-3423, by Bessadok and Grisoni, **on**
    TxGNN — [39322717](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39322717/), pages 3601-3613 of the same issue — and its reference
    list cites that paper directly. It was carded as a model in its own right
    because its title is nearly a copy of the title it discusses, which is the
    same failure as the *Cell* preview in April, eight months earlier in this
    same corpus. Its card is now `neutral` and typed `commentary`.

!!! note "What 2024 was for"
    Twelve months were added to test five "first appearance" claims. All five
    moved earlier, and eight of thirteen threads now open in 2024-01 — the first
    month that exists. The correct reading of that is not that 2024 was where
    things started. It is that this instrument cannot date beginnings, only
    floors, and it should stop trying.
